role.altitude: The health information technologist keeps judging access, pulling and scanning old records, training staff and owning the hospital's queries; checking treatment relations by hand, logging retrievals, writing first drafts of SQL and testing by eye shrink.
skills_to_grow: Keeping reference results and the data dictionary current so drafted and changed queries can be checked
role.ambitious_version: A records team that serves every record request the same day and changes a report query in an afternoon with tests to prove it.

tasks.short: Take requests, check the requester's treatment relationship, retrieve patient medical records from the archive or other providers, scan and link paper records to the electronic record, and log and return the records.

steps.what: Physicians or outpatient secretaries request old or external patient records: by mail today, on a form in the electronic record after the change
Health information technologist checks that the requester has a treatment relationship with the patient
Health information technologist retrieves the patient medical records from the paper archive or the scanned archive
Health information technologist scans paper records and links them to the patient and document type in the electronic record
Health information technologist prepares requests for records from other hospitals or the GP: by e-mail today, through the exchange where the provider is connected after the change
Health information technologist checks each external request: patient, records asked for, the treatment relationship behind it and the provider it goes to
Health information technologist sends the checked request to the other provider
Health information technologist files the external records that arrive under the patient and document type
Health information technologist logs each retrieval and returns paper records to the archive

tasks.design: Requests come in on a form in the electronic record ({OPS_SYSTEM}) instead of by mail. The form checks the requester's treatment relationship against the patient's appointments and admissions, and only exceptions go to the technologist. Each request prints a barcode cover sheet, so a scanned paper record lands under the right patient and document type. The technologist checks each external request before sending it once; requests go and records arrive through the hospital's exchange with other providers where they are connected. The request system logs every status change. Pulling and scanning paper stay physical work.

approvals.approved_version: Each request with patient, records asked for and the treatment relationship exactly as checked by the technologist in s5b, sent once to the named hospital or GP, through the exchange or by e-mail; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Requests came by mail and every step was logged by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Request forms in hospital records, barcode scanning and electronic exchange between providers.
tasks.still_hard: Old paper records that were filed wrongly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing where a record from a merged hospital ended up.
tasks.altitude: Less checking and logging; access decisions on exceptions stay with the technologist.

reach.learn: Whether records arrive before the consultation more often.

evidence.claim: Health data are special category; access must be limited to those treating the patient.
The medical record must be kept twenty years.
Hospital records check treatment relations and link scanned documents by barcode.

assumptions: Boundary: from request to records available and logged; release of copies to patients is a separate task.

Input contract for s2: appointments and admissions in the electronic record, entered by planning staff as today; about 80% of requests match a relationship; the rest are checked by hand; s2 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s4: the barcode cover sheet printed from the request record in s1.

Input contract for s5 and s5f: about a third of external requests go to providers connected to electronic exchange; s5 and s5f keep 70. The check and the send keep their full time. Retrieving records (s3) keeps its full time because pulling paper and finding scans do not change; s6 keeps 30 for returning paper records.
Requester time is outside the technologist's savings.
unknowns: How much of the paper archive is still in use.
research_questions: Do misfiled scans fall with barcode cover sheets?

already_counted.description: Health information technologist decides requests the relationship check refuses.

incremental.description: Health information technologist keeps document types on cover sheets current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: appointments are often missing for the requester, so more requests are checked by hand, and cover sheets are often not used, so s2 keeps 80 and s4 keeps 90 (16.7); high: about 80% of requests match as assumed (25.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan training for new staff and changes, prepare work instructions, train medical records staff, audit their work and give feedback, and record completed training.

steps.what: Health information technologist plans training for new staff and for coding rule or system changes
Health information technologist prepares training materials and work instructions

loop.input: The system release notes or coding rule change, and the current work instruction it affects.
loop.output: A draft revised work instruction with the changed steps marked.
loop.check: Every changed step must cite the release note item or coding manual section it follows from, or it is marked; the technologist reads each changed step against the cited item to check it says the same, rewrites what does not and writes new material by hand; no patient data are used.
loop.why_not_simpler: Release notes describe the system; staff need the steps of their own work.

steps.what: Health information technologist checks the final work instruction: each step against the release note or coding manual, and the staff group it is meant for
Health information technologist publishes the checked work instruction to medical records staff
Health information technologist trains medical records staff on the job and in sessions
Health information technologist audits a sample of staff work and gives feedback
Health information technologist records who completed which training

tasks.design: When a system release or coding rule changes, a bounded step drafts the revised work instruction from the release notes and the current instruction, citing each change; the technologist reads each change against its source, edits it, checks the final instruction and publishes it once. Audit samples of staff work are drawn by a fixed rule from the coding worklist. Completion is recorded in the hospital's {LMS} when staff finish the e-learning or are signed off. Training and feedback stay face to face.

approvals.approved_version: The work instruction exactly as checked by the technologist in s2b, published once to the medical records staff it is meant for; any change needs a new check.

tasks.previous_blocker: Work instructions were rewritten by hand after every release.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that draft revised instructions with citations, and LMS completion records.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining why a code is wrong in a way a new coder remembers.
tasks.altitude: Less writing of materials; training stays in person.

reach.learn: Whether updated instructions cut questions after releases.

evidence.claim: A Dutch hospital data body runs a coding model whose below-threshold cases go to a coder's worklist with audit samples.
Per-person audit results can monitor staff and need works council consent if used to judge them.

assumptions: Boundary: training medical records staff; hiring is separate.
Input contract for s2: release notes from the record system's supplier and the coding manual; no patient records go into the drafting step.
Input contract for s5: completion records written by the {LMS} when e-learning is finished or the trainer signs off.

Training sessions, planning, the final check and publishing keep their full time. s2 keeps 70 for reading and editing the draft and writing new material; s4 keeps 80 because only drawing the sample goes; s5 keeps 40 for sign-offs the trainer records.
unknowns: Staff turnover and the number of releases per year.
research_questions: Do coding errors after a release fall?

already_counted.description: Health information technologist edits drafted work instructions.

incremental.description: Health information technologist keeps the audit sampling rule current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: release notes are thin, so drafts need much rewriting and s2 keeps 90 (8.0); high: clear release notes and frequent changes (12.6).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Take query requests, write or maintain archived procedures, procedural codes and queries for applications, test them against reference results, document them, have a colleague review them and deploy them.

steps.what: Health information technologist takes requests for new or changed queries and procedures from users
Health information technologist writes or changes the queries, stored procedures and procedural codes

loop.input: The query specification and the data dictionary of the warehouse tables; no patient data.
loop.output: A draft query or change to a stored procedure.
loop.check: The draft must run on the test database and pass the reference result tests for that query, or it goes back with the error; for a new query without reference results the technologist checks the output against the specification by hand; the technologist reads every line before review.
loop.stop: Three drafts per specification; then the technologist writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: Templates cover standard extracts; new questions need new joins and filters.

steps.what: Health information technologist tests the query on test data and checks the results
Health information technologist documents the query and its codes in the procedure register
Data colleague reviews the final query change and approves it
Health information technologist checks the change to deploy: the same code the colleague approved, what it returns, and the production database and schedule it goes to
Health information technologist deploys the approved query to production

approvals.approved_version: The query change exactly as reviewed and approved by the data colleague in s5 and checked by the technologist in s5b, deployed once to the named production database; any later edit needs a new review and check.

tasks.design: Each production query gets stored reference results on the test database, and a test run compares a changed query's output with them, so testing is mostly reading the differences. A bounded step drafts new queries from the specification and the data dictionary only, and a draft counts only if it runs and passes the tests. Documentation is filled from the query's metadata and the technologist writes the purpose and limits. A colleague reviews every change; the technologist checks the approved version and deploys it once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Queries were written from scratch and tested by comparing outputs by eye.
tasks.enabler_now: Models that draft SQL from a data dictionary, and test runs against reference results.
tasks.still_hard: Knowing what the user really means by a count.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which registration habits make the data lie.
tasks.altitude: Less writing and checking by eye; ownership of queries stays with the technologist.

reach.learn: Whether tested queries cut report corrections.

evidence.claim: Hospital data for the national dataset leave the record through a fixed module and a privacy service.
Language models can draft SQL from a table description; tests decide whether it is right.
Health data are special category, so drafting uses only the data dictionary and test data.

assumptions: Boundary: from request to query in production; using the results is the requester's work.

Input contract for s3: reference result sets per production query on pseudonymised test data, built by the technologist when a query is first tested; about 70% of queries have them; s3 is priced at that share.
Input contract for s2: the data dictionary of the warehouse kept by the data team.

Requests, review, the deploy check and deployment keep their full time; the colleague's review is outside the technologist's savings. s4 keeps 70 because tables and fields fill from metadata and the technologist writes the purpose.
unknowns: How many queries are changed per month.
research_questions: Do production query errors fall after reference tests?

already_counted.description: Health information technologist reads drafted query code and fixes it.
Health information technologist checks test differences that are expected changes.

incremental.description: Health information technologist builds and refreshes reference results for queries.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few queries have reference results yet and drafts often fail, so s2 keeps 90 and s3 keeps 85 (9.2); high: about 70% of queries with reference results (21.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
